hook.en: At the bank counter, the person who came first is served first, and newcomers join at the end. A computer queue works exactly like this line.
hook.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಕೌಂಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೊದಲು ಬಂದವರಿಗೆ ಮೊದಲು ಸೇವೆ, ಹೊಸಬರು ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ಕ್ಯೂ ಕೂಡ ಹೀಗೆಯೇ.

objectives.en: Give real-life and computer applications of queues

narration.en: At the bank counter, the person who came first is served first, and newcomers join at the end. A computer queue works exactly like this line.
narration.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಕೌಂಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೊದಲು ಬಂದವರಿಗೆ ಮೊದಲು ಸೇವೆ, ಹೊಸಬರು ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ ಕ್ಯೂ ಕೂಡ ಹೀಗೆಯೇ.

body.en: A queue is an ordered linear list of elements with two ends. New elements are added at one end, the REAR (or tail), and removed from the other end, the FRONT (or head). The element that has been in the queue the longest is removed first, so a queue follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle, also called first come first served.

points.en: Compare: a stack uses only one end (LIFO)

The element that has been in the queue the longest is removed first, so a queue follows the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle, also called first come first served.
narration.kn: ಕ್ಯೂ ಎರಡು ತುದಿಗಳ ರೇಖೀಯ ಪಟ್ಟಿ. ಹೊಸ ಅಂಶ REAR ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುತ್ತದೆ, FRONT ನಿಂದ ಹೊರಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಮೊದಲು ಬಂದದ್ದು ಮೊದಲು ಹೊರಗೆ: FIFO.

body.en: In real life: a waiting list for train tickets, where W/L1 is confirmed first; calls to a customer-care centre that are put on hold and answered in order; vehicles on a single-lane road or at a toll booth. In computers: a web server that queues requests beyond what it can serve at once, an operating system that queues jobs for the processor, and a shared printer that queues print jobs.

narration.kn: ನಿಜಜೀವನದಲ್ಲಿ: ರೈಲು ಟಿಕೆಟ್ ವೇಟಿಂಗ್ ಲಿಸ್ಟ್, ಗ್ರಾಹಕ ಸೇವಾ ಕರೆಗಳು, ಟೋಲ್ ಬೂತ್. ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ: ವೆಬ್ ಸರ್ವರ್ ವಿನಂತಿಗಳು, ಆಪರೇಟಿಂಗ್ ಸಿಸ್ಟಮ್ ಕೆಲಸಗಳು, ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಪ್ರಿಂಟರ್.

problem.en: Tokens T1, T2, T3 join a bank queue in that order. The cashier serves one customer, then T4 joins, then the cashier serves two more. Who is still waiting?

steps.en: Queue: T1, T2, T3 (FRONT = T1, REAR = T3).
Serve one → T1 leaves: T2, T3.
T4 joins at the REAR: T2, T3, T4.
Serve two → T2 and T3 leave.

answer.en: Only T4 is waiting, and it is at the FRONT.

narration.en: Let us follow the tokens as they join at the rear and leave from the front.
